subject: Business
title: Framing: Same Facts, Different Reactions
description: A fast breakdown of Framing: Same Facts, Different Reactions for builders.

hook.text: '90% fat-free' and '10% fat' are the same thing. But one sells dramatically better.

buildup.text: Framing means how information is presented changes how people respond to it.

discovery.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed doctors chose differently for the same surgery based on survival vs. death framing.

twist.text: Rational people shouldn't be swayed by wording. But we're not rational. We're human.

climax.text: Politicians frame the same tax as 'relief' or 'cut' depending on their goal. Same policy, different emotion.

punchline.text: It's not what you say. It's the frame you put around it.

quiz.question: What does framing effect mean?
options: How information is presented changes how people respond
People always choose the first option presented
Visual design matters more than content

details.summary: Framing effects show that identical information presented differently leads to opposite decisions. Describing meat as 95% lean versus 5% fat, or a treatment as having a 90% survival rate versus 10% mortality rate, produces dramatically different consumer and patient choices.
details.whyItMatters: Framing is central to marketing, negotiation, and leadership communication. Understanding that how information is presented matters as much as what is presented gives professionals a powerful tool for influence and clearer decision-making.
takeaways: Identical information framed as gain versus loss produces opposite choices
People are risk-averse for gains but risk-seeking to avoid losses
Effective communicators frame messages to match their audience's motivations

faq.question: How do marketers use framing to increase sales?
faq.answer: Marketers frame discounts as savings rather than reduced prices, subscriptions as daily costs rather than annual totals, and product features as gains rather than prevention of losses. The same offer framed differently can double conversion rates in tested campaigns.

faq.question: Can awareness of framing effects improve your decisions?
faq.answer: Reframing the same choice in multiple ways helps reveal your true preferences. If you choose differently when information is presented as a gain versus a loss, your preference is being driven by the frame rather than genuine values. This awareness improves consistency.
